com.vector.cfg.gen.core.testinfrastructure.published

Interface IGeneratorTestingAccess<T extends com.vector.cfg.gen.core.moduleinterface.IGeneratorPackage>

  • All Superinterfaces:
    IDeployablePackageTestingAccess<T>, com.vector.cfg.gen.core.moduleinterface.IGeneratorPackageReferable, com.vector.cfg.gen.core.moduleinterface.auxiliary.IHasGetGeneratorResultSink, org.junit.rules.TestRule

    @PublishedApi(value=ADDITIONS_ALLOWED)
 @PublishedApiDomain(value=AUTOMATION_IF)
 @NotThreadSafe
public interface IGeneratorTestingAccess<T extends com.vector.cfg.gen.core.moduleinterface.IGeneratorPackage>
extends com.vector.cfg.gen.core.moduleinterface.IGeneratorPackageReferable, com.vector.cfg.gen.core.moduleinterface.auxiliary.IHasGetGeneratorResultSink, IDeployablePackageTestingAccess<T>, org.junit.rules.TestRule
    IGeneratorTestingAccess
    The IGeneratorTestingAccess holds one created IGeneratorPackage under test and provides the following accessors:
    • getGeneratorPackage()
    • getGenerationProcessor()
    • getResultSink()
    The IGeneratorPackage needs to be activated before it is used in the test case. The best way to do it is with an JUnit TestRule, see listing below. You could also use the with(Closure) method. Or you do it manually with activate() and deactivate(), but you have to use a try/finally construct.

    All method parameters and return values must be non-null unless documented otherwise.

        @PublishedMethod

IGenTestingGeneratorResultSink getResultSink()
